statement: An email company tested a new spam filter on $500$ emails. $$\begin{array}{l|c|c|c} & \text{Flagged} & \text{Not flagged} & \text{Total} \\ \hline \text{Spam} & 72 & 8 & 80 \\ \text{Not spam} & 48 & 372 & 420 \\ \hline \text{Total} & 120 & 380 & 500 \end{array}$$ Of the emails the filter flagged, what percent were actually spam?

choices.misconception: I divided the 72 flagged spam emails by all 500 emails instead of by the 120 flagged emails.
I found the percent of all emails that were flagged, 120 out of 500, which ignores whether they were spam.
I divided 72 by the 80 spam emails, which tells how much spam got flagged, not how much flagged mail was spam.

hints: The question limits you to the flagged emails. How many emails were flagged?
Use the Flagged column only. What fraction of that column is spam?
$120$ emails were flagged and $72$ of those were spam.

solutions.reliable: The filter flagged $120$ emails, and $72$ of them were spam. The percent is $\dfrac{72}{120} = 0.6 = 60\%$.
solutions.elegant: Compare the two flagged groups: $72$ spam to $48$ not spam is $3 : 2$, so spam makes up $\frac{3}{5} = 60\%$ of the flagged emails.
